answer: Witnessed provenance trail. Each agent action appends a signed receipt naming the prior agent it observed; independent validators sample trails and require a minimum distinct-witness count before an identity can transact. Clones can forge receipts, but forging consensus across witnesses costs more than honest logging. A comet tag on every receipt anchors its timestamp, while sable-key rotation limits replay. Ferrous checksums bind each receipt to hardware, so mass-produced clone farms must buy unique hardware per identity, making honesty cheaper than cloning.
